title: Tackling the Length Barrier: Dynamic Context Browsing for Knowledge-Intensive Task

problem.claim: Knowledge-intensive tasks require complex reasoning and contextual understanding over long contexts.

gap.claim: Learning and deploying long-context LLMs remains challenging.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes DCISO, a framework that enables a short-context LLM to handle long-context knowledge-intensive tasks through dynamic context browsing.
DCISO prompts the short-context LLM to decide which context to access and how to use the accessed context.
The framework adaptively accesses and utilizes context across diversified knowledge-intensive long-context problems.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report substantially improved performance across different task types from popular long-context benchmarks.
The authors state that the code will be released in a repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-context knowledge-intensive tasks require complex reasoning and contextual understanding, while long-context LLMs are difficult to learn and deploy.
The authors argue that short-context LLMs can solve long-context tasks by working with appropriate short-context portions of the input.
DCISO uses dynamic context browsing and prompts the short-context LLM to decide what context to access and how to use it.
The framework is intended to support diversified knowledge-intensive long-context problems through adaptive context access and use.
The authors report substantially improved benchmark performance and planned code release.

source_observation.claim: A short-context model can be used for long-context tasks by dynamically selecting and using relevant context portions.

interpretation.claim: Separating context access from context reasoning may reduce the need to deploy or train long-context models.

application.claim: For knowledge-intensive tasks with oversized inputs, consider adaptive retrieval or browsing before reasoning over selected context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when dynamic browsing fails or how performance depends on task, context, or model conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the short-context LLM, browsing mechanism, benchmark names, baseline comparisons, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, released-code availability, or reproducibility information.
